[Verse 1]
As they sail the midnight waves,
Black glass and silver hue…
The little boy looks up in the sky
And asks “you coming moon?”
His father at the helm,
His mum pulls him in close
And begins to tell him the tales
Of the orcas of the coast
She tells of family of majestic creatures
That swim the Pacific blue,
Black dorsal fins cutting waves,
Of spy hopping to get a view.
These black and white sea creatures
Are unmatched hunters of the sea,
Yet they recognize and respect us,
Never brought a human harm.
They teach their children all they know,
Play and sing majestic songs,
And just like her little boy,
They all love their moms.
The little boy was in awe,
Entranced with his mum’s every word,
His eyes now locked on the sea
Just for a glimpse of what he had heard.
She said if he goes to the rocky shore
And calls out a name of one of their kind,
“Percyyyyyy,” would echo through the wind-
This orca’s pod he would surely find.
[Chorus]
My mum’s tales of the killer whales
Left my mind and heart aglow.
They captured my imagination
And would shape my very soul…
The way she guards,
The way she shows…
With every tale she tells at night,
My young heart starts to grow.
[Verse 2]
She tells of swells before they break,
Of currents, cold and pale,
Of shadows slipping canyon walls
Where echo rides the gale.
Their whistles crack the granite cliffs,
Their flukes in restless flight,
A streak of black and comet foam
Across the northern night.
From her I learn the narrow pass,
To trust what can’t be seen,
To hear the softer voice of truth
Inside a quiet dream.
Her careful tales, her anchored hand
Turn down my doubt to peace,
Her patient gaze, her steady laugh
Make all my tremors cease.
We chase the waves and leap for joy,
We race the flying spray,
My childish shouts, my searching eyes
Still trace her story’s way.

[Verse 3]
Years roll on like winter tides,
Those bedtime waves grow small,
But in the hush of grown-up storms
I hear her oceans call.
When questions crowd my restless mind
And every path feels wrong,
She circles back in shining words,
A lighthouse made of song.
When I feel lost on endless seas,
Her voice still names my star,
She sees the spark I can’t recall,
The truth of who we are.
And when she fades like distant surf,
I will not let her go,
Her reckless love wraps round my ribs,
My oldest undertow.
[Bridge]
Not just a story, she shapes my soul…
Our braided lives have formed a whole.
A mother surging toward the sky,
Her stories always glide.
Our pod keeps swimming through the years,
A tide that will not hide.
Along the misted northern coast
Our paths still twist and blend:
Her guiding tales, my searching eyes,
One song that never ends.
Her fire still hums when nights grow cold,
Her calm outlasts the storm,
She lifts me higher when I fall,
She keeps one lantern warm.
Along the wind I hear the call,
Stretched out and rising free-
On gray-blue air the echoes ring:
“Percyyyyyy on the sea.”
I won’t be perfect, learning too,
Still stumbling as I flow,
But stubbornly, through every swell,
I’ll stay and let love grow.
